text:
anya: quick check — ran a two-pass late-binding speculative decode on the new q4f-quant 70B onboard. saw ~2.3x token/sec vs single-pass q4f baseline but a small quality hit on math/code prompts. anyone else run this setup?

sam: nice, 2.3x is huge. what exact pipeline? two-pass as in: fast light-decoder -> rerank top-k with full model? and quant level q4f?

anya: yea — first pass = lightweight int8-ish decoder (fast scoring), collect top-16 candidates, second pass = rescoring with the q4f model in fp16 for final pick. batch=8, seq=512, no prefix-caching for this run to isolate behavior.

liam: can you paste the eval diffs? which benchmarks moved and by how much?

anya: quick numbers from the smoke eval (same seed, 1k samples):
MMLU: single-pass q4f baseline = 68.3, two-pass = 66.1 (-2.2)
GSM8K: baseline = 78.9, two-pass = 76.0 (-2.9)
HellaSwag: baseline = 86.4, two-pass = 86.0 (-0.4)
CodeBLEU (subset): baseline = 54.2, two-pass = 50.8 (-3.4)
Notes: hallucination rate on long-context factual Qs up ~1.5% absolute.

maria: ugh math/code regressions are concerning. do we know where the loss comes from — sampling / rescoring mismatch / tokenization?

anya: hypothesis: candidate generation uses a temperature and top_p tuned for speed, so candidates are narrower; rescoring on fp16 then selects among a less diverse set. also noticed rescoring uses a lightly different logit scaling due to fused-kernel differences between fast decoder and rescoring path — small calibration shift.

sam: can we try: (a) increase candidate k from 16->64, (b) relax temp/top_p on first pass, (c) run rescoring in int8->fp16 fallback to see if precision shift matters? also run a deterministic rerank (no sampling) to isolate sampling variance.

anya: queued ablations: k=[16,32,64], first-pass temp=[0.6,0.8,1.0], top_p=[0.8,0.95], rescoring mode=[fp16, int8->fp16]. will run overnight.

liam: add a focused numeric unit test set (arith chains, step-by-step) + code-synthesis prompts. we should track which prompts change label by label so we can see pattern (e.g., carries/long arithmetic).

maria: also capture kv-cache miss/hit distribution. late-binding might alter cache lifetime and make some token prefixes fall out/swap, which could affect step-by-step.

anya: good call. I'll log kv-cache hitrates and per-layer activation norms for failing examples.

eval-bot: perf artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-eval/runs/1950124860/artifacts.tar.gz (includes raw outputs + perf traces + eval summary).

sam: quick operational note — we should gate enabling two-pass for prod with a criteria: no >1.0% absolute drop on core QA (MMLU/gsm) and code metrics, otherwise can be used only for non-critical traffic. add canary flag.

anya: agreed. will prepare a canary plan and a short checklist: perf delta, ablation matrix, targeted unit tests, gating thresholds, rollback plan.

liam: can we also try a hybrid: run single-pass for numeric/code routes (router) and two-pass for free-form chat? might buy perf where quality matters.

anya: yep — plan to test router + route-specific policy. will include that in the next run.

maria: pinging eng-runtime for resource scheduling when you run 64-candidate ablation — that'll spike memory.

anya: copying @eng-runtime and @eng-platform for scheduling — will post the full ablation matrix and results tomorrow. :thumbsup:

sam: awesome, thanks anya. :rocket:
